title: Prefixes
subtitle: ex-, half-, in-, im-, non-, pre-, re-, un-
summary: Use common prefixes like un-, im-, re- and pre- to understand and build new words.

lesson.heading: What is a prefix?
lesson.text: A **prefix** comes at the beginning of a word. It changes the meaning of the word. If you know a few common prefixes, you can often guess what a new word means.

lesson.heading: ex- and half-
lesson.text: **ex-** means the person had this job or place in your life before, but not now. **half-** means 50% of something.

examples.text: An **ex-wife** is a woman who is now divorced.
An **ex-boyfriend** is someone who is no longer your boyfriend.
Something that cost £10 yesterday and costs £5 today is **half-price**.
A **half-hour** journey is a journey of 30 minutes.

lesson.heading: in-, im-, non- and un- : not
lesson.text: These four prefixes all mean **not**. Sadly there is no rule for choosing between them, so learn each word as you meet it.

examples.text: **Informal** clothes are clothes like jeans and trainers. Formal clothes are things like a suit.
If something is **impossible**, you can't do it. It's **impossible** to read with your eyes closed.
You must not smoke in a **non-smoking** restaurant.
**Unhappy** means sad, the opposite of happy.
**Unsafe** means dangerous, the opposite of safe.

left.label: pre- = before
left.text: The action or time comes before something else.
examples: **Pre-school** children are too young to go to school.
You nearly always need to **pre-heat** the oven before you cook something.
**Pre-exam** nerves are the nerves you feel before an exam.

right.label: re- = again
right.text: You do the same thing a second time.
examples: To **redo** something is to do it a second time.
To **rewrite** something is to write it a second time.
To **resend** an email is to send it again.

lesson.text: Sometimes a word with a prefix has a hyphen (*a half-hour programme*) and sometimes it does not (*an impossible question*). Check in a dictionary when you are not sure.

exercises.prompt: I can't read this. Please ___ your homework.
exercises.explanation: re- means 'again', so rewrite is 'write a second time'.

exercises.prompt: In ___ English we often say 'Hi', not 'Good morning'.
exercises.explanation: in- means 'not', so informal is the opposite of formal.

exercises.prompt: I liked school but my sister was very ___ there.
exercises.explanation: un- means 'not', so unhappy means sad.

exercises.prompt: I bought two T-shirts because they were ___ in the sale.
Don't walk on that wall - the notice says it is ___.
exercises.explanation: Unsafe means dangerous, the opposite of safe.

exercises.prompt: Match each prefix with its meaning.

exercises.statement: An ex-husband is a man who is now divorced from his wife.
exercises.explanation: Correct. ex- means 'was but now isn't'.

options: a book that has not been read
a book that someone reads again
a book you read before an exam
a book that is only half finished
exercises.explanation: un- means 'not', so an unread book is a book nobody has read.

exercises.prompt: Match each word or phrase with its meaning.

pairs.right: a brother with one parent the same
a drink with no alcohol in it
a letter that is not finished

exercises.prompt: Which prefix makes the negative of each word?
It's ___ to read with your eyes closed.
exercises.explanation: The negative of possible is impossible, with im-.

exercises.prompt: The weather was cold and wet - it was a very ___ day.
exercises.explanation: The negative of pleasant is unpleasant, with un-.

exercises.prompt: Say why these children do not go to school yet.
exercises.answer: Pre-school children are too young to go to school.
